title: Zolbetuximab-clzb Injection
overview: Zolbetuximab-clzb injection is used in combination with other medications to treat certain types of gastric adenocarinoma (stomach cancer) or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (cancer where the esophagus and stomach meet). Zolbetuximab is in a class of medications called monoclonal antibodies. It works by stopping tumor-producing cells.

sections.Before receiving zolbetuximab-clzb,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to zolbetuximab-clzb, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in zolbetuximab-clzb injection. Ask your pharmacist or check the Medication Guide for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. If you become pregnant while receiving zolbetuximab-clzb, call your doctor. You should not breastfeed during treatment with zolbetuximab-clzb or for 8 months after your last dose.do not have any vaccinations without talking to your doctor.you should know that zolbetuximab-clzb has caused severe nausea and vomiting that sometimes causes your doctor to have to stop your treatment. Let your doctor know if you experience nausea and vomiting and if it continues to worsen.
sections.Zolbetuximab-clzb may cause side effects: nausea and/or vomitingdecreased appetiteweight losstirednessdiarrheatingling or numbness in arms or legsstomach painconstipationfever
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: hives, rash or swelling of face, throat, lips; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; chills or shaking; tirednesssigns and symptoms of an infection such as fever, cough, nasal congestion, difficulty or painful urination, chillsZolbetuximab-clzb may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
